subject: Hamiltonian animated gifs with R source

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Hamiltonian animated gifs with R source
parts:
(Andrew --- feel free to blog this.)

Shravan asked if I was willing to share the animations from the
talk I recently gave in Melbourne:

https://vimeo.com/ssavic/20150428-carpenter

and I realize I hadn't before. Here's the R code and 3 animated GIFs illustrating
too-large, too-small, and just-right step sizes in the Hamiltonian:

https://www.dropbox.com/sh/vobwxzt256l53jl/AAC6-ho_ESw37aNESkQlKvZHa?dl=0

I put the actual slides I used up there, too, as a pdf. There's more material
in them I didn't get to in the talk.

Michael Betancourt also has a stash of very beautiful 3D animations
for the funnel comparing Euclidean to Riemannian HMC.

My R code just uses RStan to generate potential and gradient and then
writes the Hamiltonian simulator directly in R, which it then pipes
to ggplot2 and the animation package.

As much as I gripe about R, it makes this kind of thing easy.

Another thing that could be done is to jointly illustrate the momentum
in a parallel plot and then also the Hamiltonian itself. Then it'd
look like Radford Neal's plots in the paper in the MCMC Handbook, only
animated.

- Bob
